class.name: ShapeCastResult
class.brief_description: The result of a shape cast operation.
class.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i].[/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] The result of a shape cast operation, used by [ShapeCast3DDirect]. This is significantly more optimized than the [Dictionary] return value from the corresponding shape query method of [PhysicsServer3D] when pre-allocated and reused, as it avoids the need to allocate new data. Instead, this existing object can simply be edited in place to store new results.

method.name: clear
method.description: Resets the contents of this result back to the initial state that it had when it was first created.

method.name: copy_to
method.description: Copies this result into another result. This is typically useful when providing this result to a consumer which may modify it or store it themselves, to prevent those modifications from affecting this instance.

members.member: This returns the collision-safe fraction from the first result. This is the highest percentage of the cast's motion can be applied [i]without[/i] actually colliding with the object.

This returns the collision-unsafe fraction from the first result. This is the smallest percentage of the cast's motion that can be applied in order to just barely, but consistently, cause a collision.

The [Object] that was hit by the shape, if it could be resolved. The [PhysicsServer3D] allows attaching object IDs (see [member hit_object_id]) to physics objects. This is how Godot tracks the object here.

The object ID assigned by the physics server to the physics object. Godot natively uses this to associate a node (like [PhysicsBody3D] or [Area3D]) to a low-level physics object, but this ID may also be a custom value with meaning specific to the game.
This is [code]true[/code] if the ray hit something, or [code]false[/code] if it missed.
The normal of the intersection, which is the axis that the intersection occurred along relative to the hit object.
The point at which the first intersection was detected. For intersections with mathematical perfection, this is the first point that was successfully tested, which has an undefined order.
The linear velocity of the cast shape at the [member intersection_point].
The [RID] of the physics object that was hit. This can be used to perform low level operations via the [PhysicsServer3D].
The index of the shape within the physics object that was hit, because physics objects can have multiple shapes within them.
